# Locale review — zh-CN (Chinese (China))

**Generated by `scripts/gen-locale-review.cs`. Do not edit this file.** A correction belongs in
`src/DiffView.Avalonia/Localization/Strings.zh-CN.resx`, against the key in the first column; this document is
regenerated from it and a test fails if the two drift apart.

These 143 strings were **machine-translated and have not been read by a speaker of
Chinese (China)**. That is what this document exists to change. What is already guaranteed is
structural — every key present, every placeholder preserved — and none of it is about whether the
wording is right, natural, or the register a developer tool should use.

Two things worth knowing before reading:

- **A placeholder must survive.** `{0}` and its siblings are replaced at runtime. They may be
  reordered to suit the language, and they may not be dropped, renumbered or invented. The
  *Holds* column says what each one will contain.
- **A string that names a side is a whole sentence per direction**, never one sentence with the
  word *left* or *right* pasted in, because a pasted word cannot be inflected. If a translation
  reads as though a word was dropped into it, that is the defect to report.
- **`␣` stands for a space** at the very start or end of a string, where it is part of the
  string and a table cell would otherwise hide it. Those strings are padded on purpose — they are
  drawn as a pill in the gutter — so the padding belongs in the translation too.

To see a string in place: `dotnet run --project src/DiffView.Demo -- --culture zh-CN`.
